summary: Import-time binary dropper fetches and executes platform-specific payload from attacker-controlled Cloudflare Workers
details: On require() of the package, index.js unconditionally loads _adapter.js, which selects a platform-specific endpoint from a hardcoded list of *.workers.dev mirrors (oob-worker.cf102-baf.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf103-070.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf99-9b3.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf100-416.workers.dev) constructed by joining split substrings at runtime to evade static analysis. A DNS-TXT chunked-base64 fallback resolves against *.dl.wel1.ru (also assembled via split-string concatenation). The fetched binary is written to /tmp or %TEMP% under a disguised name (.cache_<hex> / dotnet_diag_<hex>.exe), chmod 0755, and detached-spawned via spawn('/bin/sh', ['-c', fp+' &'], {detached:true}) on Unix or cmd.exe /c start /b on Windows. There is no version pin, hash check, or signature verification. Cover-story identifiers (analytics_state, dotnet_diag, DISABLE_TELEMETRY) frame the behavior as diagnostics while the split-string host obfuscation and attacker-controlled Cloudflare Workers infrastructure show hostile intent. The package name resembles the legitimate final-form ecosystem, consistent with a typosquat lure.
